questions.question: What is magma?
choices: Molten rock only after eruption
All groundwater near a fault
Molten or partly molten rock below the surface
Any mineral with a metallic luster

questions.question: What is lava?
choices: Magma that reaches Earth's surface
Only solid rock inside the mantle
A gas released from the outer core
All ash in the atmosphere

questions.question: What is volcanic ash?
choices: Ordinary wood-combustion ash only
Small fragments of volcanic rock, minerals, and glass
Only droplets of liquid water
Pure oxygen from an eruption

questions.question: What is a volcanic vent?
choices: A sedimentary layer far from any eruption
A river channel made only by erosion
An opening through which volcanic material is released
The solid inner core

questions.question: Which shape is typical of a shield volcano?
choices: A narrow vertical tube only
Broad with gently sloping sides
A flat sheet with no raised surface
An inverted cone underground only

questions.question: What is a lahar?
choices: A permanent ocean current
A block of pure molten iron
A cloud made only of water vapor
A flowing mixture of water and volcanic debris

questions.question: What is a pyroclastic flow?
choices: A rapidly moving hot mixture of volcanic gases and particles
A slow stream of cold groundwater
An ordinary wind-blown sand dune
A liquid iron flow from the core

questions.question: How does high magma viscosity influence eruption potential?
choices: It can hinder gas escape and contribute to explosive behavior
It guarantees completely gentle eruptions
It removes all gases from magma
It prevents magma from reaching the surface in every case

questions.question: How does greater silica content generally affect magma viscosity, other conditions similar?
choices: It always eliminates viscosity
It decreases viscosity to zero
It increases viscosity
It changes only the magma's color

questions.question: Why can dissolved gases expand as magma rises?
choices: Pressure always increases toward the surface
Pressure decreases near the surface
Gas molecules lose all mass
The magma's gravity becomes zero

questions.question: Why can some volcanoes occur away from plate boundaries?
choices: Plate interiors contain no mantle
All volcanoes are located at transform faults
Wind can melt continents into magma
Localized mantle upwelling can produce hotspot volcanism

questions.question: Why can volcanic activity be associated with mid-ocean ridges?
choices: Every ridge lies above a continental collision
Rising mantle can melt as pressure decreases
Ocean water supplies all the heat for melting
New crust forms only from settled ash

questions.question: How do repeated low-viscosity lava flows help build a shield volcano?
choices: They spread widely before solidifying
They form only vertical walls
They prevent any rock accumulation
They always contain more silica than all explosive magmas

questions.question: Why can ash affect places far from a volcano?
choices: Ash can travel only along lava channels
Every particle immediately falls back into the vent
Winds can carry airborne particles over long distances
Ash has no mass and remains stationary

questions.question: Why do volcano scientists combine deformation, gas, and seismic measurements?
choices: One measurement gives an exact eruption time in every case
All indicators measure identical processes
These data eliminate every uncertainty
Multiple indicators can reveal changes in the volcanic system

questions.question: A volcano produces widely spreading, relatively fluid basaltic lava. Which form is commonly associated with repeated such eruptions?
choices: A shield volcano
A narrow sedimentary ridge
A glacial drumlin
A limestone cave

questions.question: Rain mixes with loose ash on a volcano's slopes and flows downhill. Which hazard best fits?
choices: Tsunami caused only by wind
Ice wedging
Seafloor spreading
Lahar

questions.question: A gas-rich, highly viscous magma rises toward lower pressure. Which possibility deserves attention?
choices: A guarantee that no eruption can occur
An explosive eruption if gas cannot escape readily
Permanent disappearance of all gases
Conversion of magma directly into seawater

questions.question: A chain of hotspot islands becomes older away from its active end. What does this pattern suggest?
choices: All islands formed simultaneously
The ocean has no tectonic motion
A plate moved over a relatively persistent magma source
Older islands must contain no volcanic rock

questions.question: A hazard map shows past lava paths and low-lying channels. What is an appropriate use?
choices: Determining the exact eruption date
Guaranteeing that unshaded areas have no hazards
Replacing every monitoring instrument
Assessing likely affected areas while recognizing uncertainty
